clue.text: Evil male set straight

parts.note: to align something is to put it in a straight line

explanation.surface: A wicked man is being put right, as if by a reformer.
explanation.definitionFit: Malign as an adjective means harmful or malevolent, a close synonym of wicked.

clue.text: Calculated amount of old drink certainly consumed

indicators.note: the drink swallows the other word, so it goes inside

parts.note: mead is the honey drink of old; the clue speaks of a quantity of it
sure, as in 'sure, I'll come', means certainly

explanation.surface: A careful measure of an ancient brew has definitely been drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calculated amount' looks like one phrase, but only 'Calculated' defines; mead is the honey wine drunk in the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured or calculated response is one that is deliberate and carefully weighed.

clue.text: Some meal uncharged? It never is

definitions.text: Some meal uncharged? It never is

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'there's no such thing as a free lunch' makes the whole clue the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunch is a midday meal, and the proverb says nobody ever gets one truly free of charge.

clue.text: Bold impudence supported by soldier, possibly

a soldier ant is one caste of ant, so an ant may be a soldier

explanation.surface: Daring cheek backed up by a fighting man.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant means brave and spirited, a synonym of daring.

clue.text: Unsystematic piece needed to complete memo, as we hear?

explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, MEMORANDUM is 'memo random'; take away 'memo' and the piece left is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random follows no plan or method, which is what unsystematic describes.

clue.text: Charles de Gaulle, for instance, as seen in fair portrait

indicators.note: the answer can be seen sitting inside the next two words

parts.note: the answer runs from the second letter of the first word into the second word

explanation.surface: The French president looks well in a flattering painting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the man himself, but Charles de Gaulle is also the main Paris airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris-Charles de Gaulle is an example of a major international airport, named after the statesman.

clue.text: From which setter may be identified?

explanation.surface: A question about how one might tell who a crossword compiler is.
explanation.walkthrough: Several crossword setters have been clergy, so the clerical collar fits the compiler reading too.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog collar is both the band round a pet's neck and the stiff white collar a cleric wears.

clue.text: Removed silver, say, over time — how a lot of money's made

indicators.note: the first word lies over the other, covering it all round

explanation.definitionFit: Coins are minted, struck at the Mint, so money is produced this way; minted also means rich.

clue.text: Indication of challenge that may be punishing for runner

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a punishment of being beaten while passing between two lines of men

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a challenger's glove and the double row of attackers an offender had to run between.

clue.text: Awfully thrilled to set about European champion

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Cross river, then getting over the hill?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb about the river, but it is the definition, meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging means furiously angry, a stronger form of being annoyed.

clue.text: Acknowledgment of being hit endlessly — that hurts!

explanation.walkthrough: Touché, from fencing, loses both its end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is the exclamation of sudden pain, what someone shouts when something hurts.

clue.text: One who needs stars for casting

clue.text: Organised in units, go crazy

mental is informal British slang for mad

clue.text: Like any of us, cut by current attack on reputation

clue.text: Any power that's possessed the means to fight

clue.text: Capes put on after concert by right people

taken as written

clue.text: Stone's remixed old record for dance

clue.text: Drawing aid from head of state
